purpose: Teach: 松岡/呉/伊東/藤沢/永井/尾崎/黒田/英寿

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがTOKIOの松岡さん出演番組を観られた
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to watch that TOKIO show with Matsuoka on it.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic. Settling into a memory. Slight pause before the name, as if seeing him there. Warm but distant, the way old people drift into the past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、広島県呉の海軍記念館に行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm-hmm. And you went to the naval museum down in Kure, didn't you, dear? Back when you were young.
lines.style: Gentle correction-that's-not-quite-right. Testing memory together rather than correcting. Affectionate tilt on 'dear'. The ease of people who've spent decades in the same room.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが伊東温泉に新婚旅行に行かれた
lines.en: Your father took a honeymoon trip to Ito Hot Springs when he was young, remember.
lines.style: Drifting further back. Even quieter now. The cadence of someone speaking across time itself, not quite to the present moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、藤沢周平の小説を愛読されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were devoted to Fujisawa Shuhei's novels back then, weren't you? That's what I remember.
lines.style: Warm counterpoint. She's weaving in her own threads now. Not correcting — conversing with the past they both inhabited. Knowing nod underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが永井荷風の随筆を蔵書された
lines.en: When he was young, your father collected essays by Nagai Kafu.
lines.style: Voice grows even thinner. Each memory now a small gift being placed down carefully. Barely above a whisper, but steady.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、尾崎豊さんの追悼番組を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You watched that memorial program for Ozaki Yutaka when you were young. I remember you were quite moved by it.
lines.style: Reaching back to hold him there. Softer than before — this one matters. Slight thickness in the voice, acknowledging what they've both lost, what they remember losing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが広島カープの黒田投手を応援された
lines.en: Your father always rooted for Kuroda when he pitched for the Hiroshima Carp.
lines.style: One of the last ones. Voice almost translucent now. The smallest smile underneath — the devotion of a father, remembered by his son.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、サッカーの中田英寿さんの試合を観られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you saw Nakada Hideto play soccer, didn't you, my dear. Such a player he was.
lines.style: Closing out gently. Warmth returns — holding his hand in the present while honoring what's past. The intimacy of an ending that isn't sad because they're still here, still remembering together.
